**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Wheat leaf with **broad, longitudinal yellow/pale striping** running the full length of the leaf
- Green tissue remains at the lower/base portion of the leaf
- The yellowing covers most of the upper leaf surface in a stripe pattern parallel to veins
- Some necrosis/browning at the leaf tip
- The stripe is wide and diffuse, not narrow pustule rows

**Differential reasoning:**
- **Stripe_Rust**: Yellow-orange pustules in narrow stripe rows — the stripes in the test image are too broad and diffuse, lacking visible pustule rows
- **Cephalosporium_Stripe**: Causes broad yellow stripes running the full leaf length, often one or few wide stripes, turning pale/tan — this matches well with the broad yellow stripe covering most of the leaf
- **Barley_Yellow_Dwarf_Virus**: Tip yellowing, usually more uniform without stripe pattern
- **Wheat_Streak_Mosaic_Virus**: Mosaic/streak pattern more irregular

The single broad yellow stripe covering most of the leaf length while green tissue persists at the base is most characteristic of **Cephalosporium Stripe**, which is a vascular disease causing distinct longitudinal yellow stripes on wheat leaves.
